keyTakeaways: South Carolina premises liability law requires property owners to maintain reasonably safe conditions for visitors, with the highest duty of care owed to invitees such as hotel guests, restaurant patrons, and attraction visitors. Common tourist injuries in Charleston include slip-and-falls, pool accidents, balcony collapses, and foodborne illness. Out-of-state visitors can file claims in South Carolina courts. The modified comparative fault rule bars recovery at 51% or more fault, and the three-year statute of limitations (S.C. Code SS 15-3-530) applies.

faqs.question: Can I file a premises liability claim if I was injured as a tourist in Charleston?
faqs.answer: Yes. South Carolina premises liability law protects all visitors regardless of where they live. If you were injured at a Charleston hotel, restaurant, shop, or attraction because of a dangerous condition the property owner knew or should have known about, you have the right to file a claim.

faqs.question: What do I need to prove in a South Carolina premises liability case?
faqs.answer: You must show a dangerous condition existed on the property, the owner knew or should have known about it, the owner failed to fix or warn about the condition, the condition caused your injury, and you suffered actual damages.

faqs.question: How long do I have to file a premises liability claim in South Carolina?
faqs.answer: The statute of limitations is three years from the date of injury (S.C. Code section 15-3-530). However, surveillance footage is typically overwritten within 30-72 hours, so contacting an attorney immediately is essential. In Georgia, the deadline is only two years.

faqs.question: What if I was partially at fault for my injury?
faqs.answer: South Carolina follows a modified comparative fault rule. You can recover damages as long as your fault is less than 51 percent. Your recovery is reduced by your percentage of fault.

faqs.question: Can I sue a Charleston restaurant if I slipped on a wet floor?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the restaurant knew or should have known about the wet floor and failed to clean it up or place warning signs. Restaurants must regularly inspect their premises for hazards.

faqs.question: What compensation can I receive for a premises liability injury?
faqs.answer: You can recover medical expenses, lost wages, pain and suffering, loss of enjoyment of life, scarring, and emotional distress. In egregious cases, punitive damages may also be available.
